title.exam: FIFTH SEMESTER (CUFYUGP) DEGREE EXAMINATION: MODEL PAPER 4
title.subject: MATHEMATICS

sections.name: Section A
sections.rule: All Questions can be answered. Each Question carries 3 marks (Ceiling: 24 Marks)
questions: For the problem minimize $f_0(x)$ subject to $f_i(x)\le0$ and $h_j(x)=0$, define the Lagrangian and the Lagrange dual function. State the sign restrictions on the dual variables.
Show that the Lagrange dual function is concave, even when the primal problem is not convex.
Define the optimal duality gap. Distinguish between weak duality and strong duality. How can a primal feasible point and a dual feasible point certify optimality?
Write the inequalities defining a saddle point $(x^\star,\lambda^\star,\nu^\star)$ of a Lagrangian, with $\lambda\ge0$. Which variables are minimized and which are maximized?
What is complementary slackness of a dual canonical linear programming problem ?
State Slater’s condition for a convex problem with inequalities $f_i(x)\le0$ and equalities $Ax=b$. What does it imply about strong duality and dual attainment when the primal optimum is finite?

List the four groups of KKT conditions for a differentiable problem. State when these conditions are sufficient for global optimality and a constraint qualification under which they are also necessary.
Distinguish between weak alternatives and strong alternatives. State an alternative system that certifies infeasibility of $Ax\le b$, where inequalities are componentwise.
For a constraint $f(x)\preceq_K0$, in which cone must its Lagrange multiplier lie? Explain why its contribution to the Lagrangian is nonpositive at a feasible point.
For a semidefinite constraint $F(x)\preceq0$ with multiplier $Z\succeq0$, write the complementary slackness condition. Give an example with both $F(x)$ and $Z$ nonzero that satisfies this condition.

sections.name: Section B
sections.rule: All Questions can be answered. Each Question carries 6 marks (Ceiling: 36 Marks)
questions: Find the dual function of the LP minimize $c^Tx$ subject to $Gx\le h$, $Ax=b$, where $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Give the dual problem, and make the implicit equality constraints explicit.

Consider minimize $x$ subject to $x^2\le0$, with $x\in\mathbb R$. Sketch $\mathcal G=\{(x^2,x):x\in\mathbb R\}$ and $\mathcal A=\{(u,t):\exists x,\ x^2\le u,\ x\le t\}$. Derive the dual and find the primal and dual optimal values. Discuss dual attainment, Slater’s condition and strong duality.

Prove weak duality for a standard-form optimization problem without assuming convexity. If $x$ is primal feasible and $(\lambda,
u)$ is dual feasible with finite $g(\lambda,
u)$, show that $0\le f_0(x)-p^\star\le f_0(x)-g(\lambda,
u)$, assuming $p^\star$ is finite.
Prove that a pair of feasible solutions of dual canonical linear programming problems exhibit complementary slackness if and only if they are optimal solutions.

Consider minimize $\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ subject to $Gx=h$, where $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ has rank $n$ and $G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ has rank $p$. Give the KKT conditions, and derive expressions for the primal solution $x^\star$ and equality multiplier $\nu^\star$.
State and prove Farkas’ lemma in the following form: the systems $Ax\le0$, $c^Tx<0$ and $A^Ty+c=0$, $y\ge0$ are strong alternatives. You may use strong duality for linear programming.

Find the Lagrange dual of minimize $c^Tx$ subject to $Ax\preceq_K b$, where $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb R^m$ and $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is a proper cone. Make any implicit equality constraints explicit.

Derive the dual of the SDP minimize $c^Tx$ subject to $F(x)=G+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iF_i\preceq0$, where $F_i,G\in\mathbb S^k$. Assuming the primal optimal value is finite, give a sufficient strict-feasibility condition for strong duality.

sections.name: Section C
sections.rule: Answer any ONE. Each Question carries 10 marks (1x10=10 Marks)
questions: Consider minimize $x^2+1$ subject to $(x-2)(x-4)\le0$, with $x\in\mathbb R$. (a) Find the feasible set and primal optimum. Derive the dual function and solve the dual problem. (5 marks) (b) Verify the KKT conditions at the optimal primal-dual pair. Show directly that this pair is a saddle point of the Lagrangian, and identify the common primal and dual optimal value. (5 marks)

(a) For a standard-form problem with domain $\mathbb R^n$, prove that a finite saddle point of the Lagrangian over $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $\lambda\ge0$, $\nu\in\mathbb R^p$ gives primal and dual optimal solutions with zero duality gap. Do not assume convexity. (5 marks) (b) For minimize $f_0(x)$ subject to $f_i(x)\preceq_{K_i}0$, $Ax=b$, formulate the dual using $K_i^*$. Prove weak duality and derive the generalized complementary slackness conditions when finite equal primal and dual optima are attained. (5 marks)
